definitions: A scientific theory proposing that petroleum and natural gas are formed from inorganic matter deep within the Earth, rather than from the decomposition of organic matter.
The hypothesis that hydrocarbons can be generated abiogenically.
examples: Proponents of Inorganic Theory often cite the presence of hydrocarbons in deep-seated igneous rocks.
The debate between Inorganic Theory and biogenic theories continues in geology.
New research sometimes provides evidence that supports aspects of Inorganic Theory.
